title.narrative: Rethinking Sahab: Urban Greening for a Resilient and Sustainable Future

description.narrative:
Sahab, located 16 kilometers southeast of Amman, Jordan, is struggling with pressing environmental, urban, and social challenges. Rapid population growth, fueled by an influx of refugees and migrant workers, has placed immense strain on the city’s infrastructure and services. With a population exceeding 187,000 residents; including a substantial number of refugees and labor migrants; Sahab residents face deteriorating roads, an unreliable water supply, inefficient waste management, and inadequate sanitation facilities. The negative impacts of these concerns are disproportionately felt by those already marginalized, such as older persons, persons with disabilities, the urban poor and refugees. Women and girls among these groups experience even more restricted access.
The city's industrial activities have also led to severe environmental degradation and high levels of air pollution. Additionally, Sahab is increasingly vulnerable to climate change impacts risks, experiencing frequent droughts, heatwaves, and flooding that intensify the urban heat island effect. These challenges are further compounded by a lack of green spaces and disparities in access to public services, particularly affecting marginalized communities.
Despite these obstacles, Sahab has been aspiring to become the first "Green City" in the Middle East since 2015, a vision that demands significant infrastructure improvements and a commitment to sustainable urban development. However, in the absence of a structured Greening Plan to coordinate and direct necessary actions, progress toward the city’s vision has been limited over the past decade.
In response to these challenges, the Triangular Social Cooperation Concept was launched through a partnership between the Government Council of the Canton of Basel-Stadt, UN-Habitat, and the Municipality of Sahab. Inspired by the "Von Stadt zu Stadt" initiative, this project aims to create a resilient, sustainable, and healthy urban environment for all residents in Sahab by integrating urban greening strategies, building community and institutional capacities, and fostering inclusive public spaces that enhance quality of life and mitigate environmental impacts.
The project’s central objective is to develop Sahab’s first Greening Public Space Plan (GPSP), a comprehensive framework aligning with the international definition of green cities. The GPSP will unify and guide the efforts of local authorities, stakeholders, including private sector, and community members in their diversity in greening the public spaces at the city and addressing industrial pollution, urban heat island, droughts, and floods. This plan will provide a detailed roadmap to address Sahab’s infrastructural and environmental challenges, directing the development of public space projects.
The project’s primary deliverables include: 1. City-Wide Public Space Assessment Report: This report will compile the findings from the city-wide assessment, offering a detailed inventory of existing public spaces, identifying gaps, and evaluating aspects such as accessibility, quantity, quality, distribution, safety, and connectivity for all Sahab residents in their diversity. It will provide data-driven insights to guide prioritization and intervention strategies for enhancing public spaces in Sahab.
2. Green Public Space Plan: Building on the assessment results, this strategic plan will align with the international definition of green cities, providing a comprehensive framework for urban greening and increasing the green area per capita in the city. It will define typologies such as parks, community gardens, and green corridors while prioritizing key sites for intervention. The plan will prioritize key sites, suggest innovative techniques such as grey water irrigation and waste recycling, and set clear objectives to expand green space availability. Furthermore, it will include recommended policy actions to be integrated into existing local strategies, plans, and fiscal frameworks, ensuring sustainable implementation and long-term impact. This roadmap will support Sahab Municipality in its efforts to establish a greener, more livable city for all.
3. Design and Implementation of Pilot Public Space(s): One or more pilot public spaces will be developed in alignment with the Green Public Space Plan's typologies. This process will include a Site-Specific Assessment Report to identify tailored interventions, followed by the Design of Public Space(s) based on community needs, including those of women and girls, and environmental priorities. Once designed, the Implementation of Public Space(s) Design will bring these concepts to life, integrating sustainable elements such as the use of recycled plastic for public furniture, waste sorting, recycling stations, compost programmes, grey water systems, and urban agriculture, all co-designed with local residents, including women and girls in their diversity.
